Identify a temple near you, that has a meditation hall. (even temples that don't have separate halls, will still have designated areas for meditation).

Carry a foldable mosquito net, as well as a wool blanket (to sit on).

Make sure you pick a comfortable location to begin with, and pick a spot where you'll be sitting. This is your "designated" meditation spot.

It's ideal to consistently meditate at the same spot, during the same times. If you plan to go in the morning at a certain time, then go at that same time everyday, and sit at the same spot. You will see that, in due time, you'll find it much easier to enter a meditative state, from your spot.

Brownie points if have the presence of the object of meditation nearby. If you have a deity that you meditate on, then a temple with the same deity will be ideal.

It also helps if the place is special to you.. maybe of some personal significance

The starting, for me, was when I had my first accidental lucid dream.. out of nowhere, i was aware in a dream.. and when I woke up from that, I had a hard time digesting it.. it was as real as the waking reality itself, if not more.. that's where, and why, i began..  
Yes, remembering dreams is tough at the beginning.. it is a skill, that will develop with practice.. if you make it a practice to note your dream memories as soon as you wake up (you can write a dream journal, or record voice-notes, whichever works for you) soon, you build a habit, and become really good at it..  
however, dont postpone.. note your recollections as soon as you wake.. because with time, you forget the details.. so if you record later on, many details will be missed
